newsitem.title: USA: Salient sees Q2 operating loss.
newsitem.headline: Salient sees Q2 operating loss.

text.p: Salient 3 Communications Inc said on Wednesday that it second quarter losses from continuing operations to "significantly exceed" the $0.10 per share loss it reported in the first quarter.
In addition, the company said it will incur a $6.15 million charge for the write-off of in-process research and development associated with its April 1997 TEC Cellular acquisition.
The telecommunications company reported a loss of $0.01 in the second quarter of 1996.

Commenting on anticipated quarterly loss, Salient said its SAFCO subsidiary is continuing to experience the effects of product delays, particularly in the United States, as well as the restructuring of its global sales force.

Salient also said it would expand its 1995 share repurchase plan to allow the company to purchase up to one million shares in the open market. Company president Timothy Cobb said the repurchase expansion reflected Salient's optimism in its "fundamental prospects."

Along with its earnings predictions, Salient announced the close of the sale of its SRA subsidiary for $8.8 million in cash, as well as an agreement to sell its real estate complex, Green Hills Corporate Center, for $40 million.
SRA was sold to Dames & Moore Inc, a global professional services company, Salient said in a statement.
Proceeds of both the sales will be used to reduce Salient's current outstanding bank debt.
